{"context":{"boundary":"Do not claim file mutation, execution, integration, truth, or customer acceptance.","desiredUse":"Advisory rights/provenance/economic circuit design; Codex retains legal caution, implementation, and acceptance.","objective":"Design a consented contributor-knowledge and revenue-allocation circuit for TTI that preserves the user's economic intent while complying with the stated Discord platform constraints by using a separate TTI-owned contribution intake.","suppliedContext":"User intent: Discord community members should be able to contribute local experiential knowledge (example: gardening in a town), have it integrated into TTI's knowledge fabric, and earn credits or a share when the knowledge is sold into the wider Union market.
Verified current platform constraints: Discord says user content remains the user's; other users' content may not be used without consent or law. Discord's general terms prohibit selling/licensing/commercializing content or data obtained from its services. Discord Developer Policy §§17-21 prohibits disclosing API Data to monetization services; selling/licensing/commercializing API Data; mining/scraping; and using API message content to train AI without Discord express permission. A local server ToS cannot override Discord's terms.
Therefore: TTI may use Discord for discovery, identity linking, commands, and notification, but must not commercialize harvested Discord/API content. A participant may instead deliberately submit their own knowledge through a separate TTI-owned form/protocol under an explicit contribution license and profit/credit agreement; Discord can issue the link/session but the submitted content must originate at TTI's boundary.
Settlement rules: TTI alone owns its contributor agreements, knowledge contribution records, derived claim provenance, sale contracts, contributor credit ledger, and fulfillment. Durable acts are typed RMN objects with RWIL/RDF provenance. Union buyers cross an ActivityStreams/x402-priced border. Revenue is external only after receipt. Existing claim-infrastructure theory models Claim→Evidence→Provenance→Warrant→Transformations→Corrections→License→agent-readable endpoint.
